Distraction and self-soothing can help you get through a crisis until you can respond more effectively.

## Wise Mind ACCEPTS {#wise-mind-accepts}

### Activities {#activities}

Focus on a task, clean a room, watch something, read, play a game, walk, exercise, make something, spend time with someone, or choose another absorbing activity.

### Contributing {#contributing}

Volunteer, help someone, offer encouragement, give away something you no longer need, make something for another person, or do something thoughtful.

### Comparisons {#comparisons}

Compare this moment with a time you felt differently, notice how other people cope with similar difficulties, or place the current situation in a wider perspective. Use comparisons to reduce suffering, not to invalidate it.

### Emotions / Opposite Emotion {#opposite-emotion}

Choose a book, show, film, story, letter, music, or other activity that brings up an emotion different from the painful emotion you are trying to survive.

### Pushing Away {#pushing-away}

Temporarily leave the situation physically or mentally. Put the pain on an imaginary shelf, box it up for later, build a mental wall, or firmly redirect rumination. Return to the problem when you are able to respond effectively.

### Thoughts {#thoughts}

Count objects or colours, repeat the words of a song, work a puzzle, read, or give your mind another neutral task.

### Sensations {#sensations}

Use a strong but safe sensation: squeeze a rubber ball, listen to loud music at a safe volume, hold ice briefly, step into rain or snow, or take a hot or cold shower.

## Self-Soothing with the Five Senses {#self-soothing-five-senses}

### Vision {#vision}

Look closely at stars, nature, art, a candle flame, a sunrise or sunset, a pleasing room, or any sight that helps you slow down. Attend mindfully to each thing you see.

### Hearing {#hearing}

Listen to soothing or energizing music, sounds of nature or the city, radio, singing, humming, or an instrument. Let sounds come and go without holding on to them.

### Taste {#taste}

Choose a favourite food or soothing drink, peppermint, gum, or a small special treat. Slow down and taste one thing mindfully.

### Smell {#smell}

Use a favourite soap, lotion, scented candle, coffee, cinnamon, flowers, fresh air, or the smell of a wooded place. Breathe in the scent mindfully.

### Touch {#touch}

Take a warm bath or shower, pet an animal, soak your feet, use lotion, wrap up in a blanket, put clean sheets on the bed, hug someone safe, or notice another soothing physical sensation.

##### Exercise 1: Self-Soothing

Self-soothing is about comforting, nurturing and being kind to yourself. Think of activities that involve your five senses, and remember to practice using these even when you are not distressed, so that you will remember to use them when you are in a crisis. In the table below, write down the activities you can use to help you feel comforted. Senses to be soothed My activities to help me feet nurtured or comforted

*e.g. look at the ocean, a favourite picture*

##### Taste
